newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak BSE changes structure of SAX index.
newsitem.headline: Slovak BSE changes structure of SAX index.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) raised the number of shares in its SAX index to 16 from 12 to reflect market activity, a BSE official said on Wednesday.

"The ratio of the index capitalisation has increased to 76 percent from 60 percent of the whole bourse capitalisation," Olga Dlugopolska, head of the BSE marketing and analytical department told Reuters.

From February 4, BSE and Creditanstalt Securities, which jointly manage the SAX, added drug company Slovakofarma, aluminium producer ZSNP, construction company Vahostav, paint maker Chemolak and wire producer Drotovna to the index.
At the same time, they dropped textile company Ozeta.
"In changing the index, we took account first of the volume of trades made in the issues over the last year," Dlugopolska said.
"While Ozeta's performance weakened, the new index members showed a constant increase in their volumes of trades and in liquidity," she said.
Oil refiner Slovnaft remains the biggest component of the SAX, accounting for 24.29 percent of the index.
The SAX, which is adjusted for changes in the capital of issuers and their dividend payments, closed 0.27 point lower at 185.82 points on Tuesday.
Dlugopolska said that the change of the index structure was calculated to cause no change of its value. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-521-8402
